note.title: Energy changes in reactions
note.overview: Chemical reactions transfer energy. Temperature observations, energy-level diagrams and bond-energy calculations help classify a reaction as exothermic or endothermic.
learningGoals: Recall the precise Year 8 scientific vocabulary and symbols.
Apply the idea to an unfamiliar example rather than relying on recognition.
Use the command word, show working where needed and include every mark point.
mustMemoriseRules: Exothermic reactions transfer energy to the surroundings, which usually warm up.
Endothermic reactions take in energy from the surroundings, which usually cool down.
In an exothermic profile products are at lower energy than reactants; in an endothermic profile products are higher.
Breaking bonds requires energy; making bonds releases energy.
Overall energy change = energy needed to break bonds - energy released making bonds.

commonMistakes: Saying exothermic means the reactants contain no energy.
Reversing the signs in a bond-energy calculation.
Calling a reaction endothermic merely because it needed ignition.
Giving a related fact without the defining scientific point.
It transfers energy only as sound.
detailedExplanation: Chemical reactions transfer energy. Temperature observations, energy-level diagrams and bond-energy calculations help classify a reaction as exothermic or endothermic.

examTips: State the direction of energy transfer, not only the temperature change.
On a profile, compare product and reactant energy levels.
Write break minus make before substituting values.
Use the command word and number of marks to decide how many distinct points are required.
Use precise terminology and link cause to effect rather than listing disconnected facts.
For calculations, show the relationship, substitution, working and unit.
